domains.applies_when: The content changes the status of a booking, publishes a booking event, or consumes one.
domains.description: Events that booking-service publishes when a booking changes, and the code that consumes them.
domains.not_applies_when: The content does not change booking status and does not publish or consume booking events.
domains.title: Booking domain events

rfcs.applies_when: The content changes the status of a booking, publishes a booking event, or consumes one.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content does not touch booking status or booking events.
rfcs.summary: booking-service publishes an event for every booking status change, through the transactional outbox, with no personal data.
rfcs.title: Booking lifecycle events

statements.applies_when: the content sets or updates the status of a booking or confirmation.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not touch booking status or booking events.
statements.text: Code that changes the status of a booking MUST enqueue a `booking.<new-status>` event with `outbox.enqueue` inside the same database transaction as the status change.
statements.title: Every status change publishes an event

statements.applies_when: the content builds the payload of a booking event.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not touch booking status or booking events.
statements.text: Booking events MUST contain only the booking id, restaurant id, new status and timestamp, and MUST NOT contain guest names, emails or phone numbers.
statements.title: Events carry identifiers only

statements.not_applies_when: The content does not touch booking status or booking events.
statements.text: Consumers of booking events SHOULD process each event id at most once.
statements.title: Idempotent consumers
